from.place: Upstream master declaration AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.CondensedRing.smoothPurityIso (#1461); the Qlb case of the blueprint theorem for the unit object

title: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.CondensedRing.smoothPurityIso
statement: Let l be a prime and k a field of characteristic p>0 with p != l. Let X, Y be separated schemes of finite type over Spec k (objects of Over (Spec k)) and f:X->Y a morphism over k whose underlying morphism of schemes is smooth of pure relative dimension d. Write Qlb for the condensed ring Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj l, Qlb_Y for the tensor unit of the monoidal category D^b_c(Y)[[Qlb]] of bounded constructible module objects over Qlb on the pro-etale site of Y, Rf^! for boundedConstructibleUpperShriek (the right adjoint of Rf_!, built from a Nagata compactification of f), and Qlb_X(d) for the Tate twist tateTwistDerived X l d of WeilConjectures.TateTwist.ProEtale [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists]. Then there is an isomorphism (Rf^! Qlb_Y) ~= Qlb_X(d)[2d] in D(Mod_{Qlb_X}) (after the fully faithful inclusion of D^b_c(X)[[Qlb]]). The upstream declaration is a chosen isomorphism (data, @[no_expose]). Its intended SGA normalization is obtained by reconstructing the inverse finite-coefficient smooth-purity comparisons, extending coefficients to the finite-extension-valued condensed Qlb ring, and identifying Lf^* of the unit with the unit. The common-stage Qlb category of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] and the condensed-module category are related by coefficient realization, not identified by definition.

proof.text: Keep the original field k and the actual target coefficient category. Put B_T=p_T^*underline(Omega), Omega=Qbar_l, for T=X,Y; here underline(Omega) is the finite-extension-valued condensed ring Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ell, not the ring of all continuous Omega-valued functions. Use the archived full bounded constructible module-object categories C^c_Omega(T) described in [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. The coefficient unit B_Y in degree zero belongs to this category: on the single stratum Y it is the cokernel of the zero map from a rank-zero free module to a rank-one free module. It has Tor amplitude [0,0], since B_Y tensor^L_{B_Y} N=N for any module sheaf N. Fix the same Nagata compactification c=(j,g) as the target, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. In the notation of [lem-pur-condensed-exceptional-reconstruction], G is the chosen boundedConstructibleUpperShriek, the composite of the chosen proper right adjoint and open restriction, with its composite adjunction. This is exactly the functor specified in that theorem, rather than a common-stage exceptional functor. All schemes in the compactification are separated finite type over k by the setting node. They are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field has only its zero and unit ideals; they have finite dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. The same hypotheses apply to the finite-type geometric constructions below. The integer ell is invertible on these schemes because char(k) differs from ell. The target has d in N. No finite-field or algebraic-closure condition on k is imposed.

source.place: Lines 76-92: exact ground field, condensed coefficient unit, chosen adjoint and target signature; existing comparison theorem fixes the same functor

proof.text:
Compute the finite-coefficient dualizing object over the original arbitrary field k, without applying sk-thm-sp-qbar: its current statement assumes k is an algebraic closure of a finite field. For n>=1 put A_n=Z/ell^n. Ordinary etale compact supports have the right adjoint f_n^times of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. By [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] its unit value omega^et_{f,n}=f_n^times A_{n,Y} is a rank-one sheaf shifted by [2d]. The comparison [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] applies over all Noetherian bases. In the Cartesian square W=X times_Y X with projections p_1,p_2 and bottom arrow f, it gives p_2^*omega^et_{f,n} -> omega^et_{p_1,n}. Pulling its inverse back by Delta gives
 C_n(p_1,Delta)=Delta^*omega_{p_1,n} -> Delta^*p_2^*omega_{f,n} -> omega_{f,n}.
Here on the pro-etale site omega_{h,n}=nu^*(h_n^times A_n). This is the finite exceptional construction specified in [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons], for the arbitrary field k, with its geometric units, counits and etale-origin equivalence. Full faithfulness and compact-support comparison are also stated in [sk-prop-sf-comparison, lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. The symbols C and the finite coefficient conventions used here are defined in [sk-def-purity-conv], which imposes ell invertible and does not restrict k to an algebraic closure of a finite field. The preservation clause of [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons] ensures that these finite exceptional functors take bounded constructible finite-Tor objects to objects of the same category. The coefficient unit is in it by the one-stratum rank-one description and Tor calculation of Step 1, now with B_Y replaced by A_{n,Y}. In particular all displayed unit values are bounded constructible, so the site comparisons apply. More explicitly, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] supplies etale-origin models K_0,L_0 for finite constructible inputs. The Hom identifications are
 Hom_proet(Rf_!K,nu_Y^*L_0) = Hom_et(Rf_!^et K_0,L_0) = Hom_et(K_0,f_n^times L_0) = Hom_proet(K,nu_X^*f_n^times L_0).
The first and last use the full faithfulness and compact-support comparisons just cited. The smooth tensor formula and the local rank-one description ensure the right-hand output remains bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Thus this is the constructible finite adjoint. Its comparison with any of the chosen constructible adjoints in the coefficient statements is the counit-preserving one of [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]; their coefficient maps coincide because those maps are defined by the same counit-mate equation.

By [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion], Delta is regular of codimension d with normal bundle N=T_{X/Y}. The current [sk-thm-dnc], stated for a smooth map with a closed section with ell invertible, gives the DNC isomorphism
 D_n:C_n(p_1,Delta) -> C_n(pi_N,0_N).
To compute its target, trivialize N over affine open subsets U of X. Apply [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] to pi_N and U->X, and pull back along the zero section, to identify C_n(pi_N,0_N)|_U with C_n(pi_{N|U},0_{N|U}); use the same canonical comparisons on overlaps. On each chart [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction] supplies the ordinary etale affine-space adjunction. Choose its explicit coordinate-tower normalization from [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. Right-adjoint uniqueness [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] compares that adjunction with pi_N^times; pull its unit-value comparison back by the zero section. This gives C_n(pi_N,0_N)|_U -> A_{n,U}(d)[2d]. On overlaps, the two charts differ by an invertible linear matrix. By [lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance] the coordinate counits are equal under that change, so the counit-preserving uniqueness comparison gives the same map in both charts. All objects, after shifting by [-2d], are locally free rank-one sheaves; therefore the agreeing ordinary sheaf maps glue, as do their inverses. Write the resulting isomorphism as v_n:C_n(pi_N,0_N)->A_{n,X}(d)[2d]. The Tate pullbacks in this calculation are those of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. For d=0 the affine-space adjunction, tensor power and chart comparison are identities.

Let j_n:C_n(p_1,Delta)->omega_{f,n} be the diagonal base-change map above. The composite delta_n=v_n o D_n o j_n^{-1}:omega_{f,n}->A_{n,X}(d)[2d] is an isomorphism; set gamma_n=delta_n^{-1}. This is the diagonal/DNC construction, not a trace-route smooth-purity input. Every scheme used is separated finite type over k, hence Noetherian; all the ordinary etale right adjoints are taken at the chosen compactifications or their base changes.

source.place: Steps 1-2: diagonal section, DNC and normal bundle; use the existing arbitrary-Noetherian ordinary-etale interfaces and the current generic sk-thm-dnc statement

proof.text:
Check compatibility of these actual maps with A_r -> A_n for every r>=n>=1. Use the finite coefficient extensions of [sk-def-sp-scalar-extension] and the compact-support and exceptional comparisons b,c of [sk-lem-sp-reduction], in its stated arbitrary-field setting. The latter specifies c by the equation epsilon_n F_n(c)=(epsilon_r)_n b^{-1}. These are the comparisons for the same geometric finite functors as in Step 2. For these specific chosen finite adjoints, [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons] supplies the same counit-defined coefficient mates, their quotient and mixed coherences, and their identification with the ordinary-etale construction used in Step 2. The simultaneous geometric section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] give the coefficient, base-change and composition diagrams before passage to homotopy categories. Alternatively their mate equalities can be checked by transposing: applying either order of coefficient extension and geometric base change to a counit gives the same composite of the proper/open exchange maps, hence the two right-adjoint comparisons coincide by the adjunction bijection. For three quotient rings, both composite mates have transpose the direct compact-support coefficient comparison, so they are equal. Thus the exceptional comparisons used below satisfy the quotient cocycle.

Here are the normalization checks for the three factors delta_n. The diagonal base-change map j is a counit mate, so the preceding equality proves its coefficient square. For D, use the family comparison kappa:F->a^*C(p_1,Delta) in [sk-thm-dnc], normalized to the identity at t=1. Reduce kappa_r using c for the smooth deformation map and the pullback/tensor coefficient comparisons. It is an isomorphism with identity restriction at t=1. By the uniqueness assertion of that same DNC statement it is kappa_n. Restriction at t=0 and inversion therefore give (D_r)_n=D_n. This uses the actual locally product DNC family, and makes no assertion that an arbitrary lisse sheaf on A^1 is constant.

For v use its specified affine coordinate normalization, not an arbitrary affine-space adjunction. In rank one [def-amb-p1-trace] defines the projective-line trace by t_q=pr_2 b_q^{-1}, where the two components of b_q are the shifted twisted unit and the Kummer first Chern class of O(1). The supported Cartier/Kummer maps commute with every coefficient reduction by [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], including their ordinary etale witnesses. The unit and proper coefficient comparison are the geometric ones just considered. Hence reduction carries both components of b_q to the corresponding components over A_n, carries its inverse to that inverse, and carries pr_2 to pr_2; it therefore carries t_q to t_q at level n. The affine-line counit is obtained from this one by the open-extension adjunction, and the d-dimensional counit is its ordered composite as specified in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. The same geometric coefficient comparisons preserve those operations and composites. Thus the affine-space counits reduce to their level-n counits. The counit-preserving uniqueness comparison used for v then reduces to that at level n. Linear-coordinate invariance gives the agreeing comparisons on overlaps, so (v_r)_n=v_n globally.

It follows by composing these three checked squares and taking inverses that c_{r,n} o (gamma_r tensor^L A_n)=gamma_n after the canonical reduction of A_r(d)[2d] to A_n(d)[2d]. The root-power and Tate reductions here follow from [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback, lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]; one may use a common exponent ell^r before extending coefficients. The quotient cocycle follows from the mate cocycle already proved and tensor associativity. Since gamma_n and its inverse satisfy the same squares, these are isomorphisms of the finite unit-value diagrams, not just unrelated isomorphisms at each level.

source.place: Coefficient mate equation; the explicit geometric and DNC normalization calculation here expands the finite-reduction step of the lecture-notes route without using the fixed-finite-field purity theorem

proof.text:
Reconstruct only the value at the coefficient unit. Put Rhat_T=lim_n A_{n,T}, L=Rhat_Y in degree zero, and Z=lim_n mu_{ell^n,X}. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], Z is locally free of rank one over Rhat_X, has the specified finite reductions and is derived complete. Use the strict tower and normalization conventions of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower], with A=Z_l and I=(ell). The coefficient facts in [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] verify the ring hypotheses: a nonzero ideal of Z_l has an element of least valuation, which divides all its elements, so every ideal is principal and Z_l is Noetherian. The quotient Z_l/ell^n is Z/ell^n, a finite ring, and the exact resolution 0 -> Z_l --ell^n--> Z_l -> Z/ell^n -> 0 makes it perfect; injectivity follows since Z_l is a subring of Q_l. In particular A/I is torsion. Also Z_l is ell-adically complete: lifts of a compatible residue system form a Cauchy sequence in the complete field Q_l, their limit has valuation at least zero and the prescribed residues, and uniqueness follows from intersection_n ell^n Z_l=0. Thus the local coefficient model N=Z_l is complete and N/ell N is finite. In the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-adic-lisse-module], the local trivializations of Z therefore exhibit Z, and each of its tensor powers, as adic lisse of finite type. Form the actual strict semilinear system M_n=A_{n,X}(d)[2d], with transitions induced by the power maps on roots of unity and their tensor powers. These maps are semilinear for A_{n+1}->A_n, and their composites are the quotient maps. The system is normalized: locally trivialize Z by the pro-etale covering supplied by the cited local-freeness statement, and the normalization becomes A_{r,X} tensor^L_{A_{r,X}} A_{n,X}=A_{n,X}; the local tensor identifications agree with the canonical root-power maps. Its global model is the degree -2d adic-lisse complex Z^{tensor_{Rhat_X}d}[2d], with d=0 meaning Rhat_X. Its finite levels are finite etale locally constant sheaves shifted by [2d]. The reconstruction theorem [lem-weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower], applied to this model and its actual quotient reduction maps, identifies the total derived limit M with that model and identifies its canonical reductions with M_n. It also gives derived completeness. These finite etale sheaves and their power transitions are compatible etale-origin witnesses, so M lies in the completed integral category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. For L use the strict unit tower A_{n,Y} in degree zero, with the quotient transitions. Its one-stratum local model is Rhat_Y in degree zero, adic lisse with complete coefficient model N=Z_l; its reductions and normalization maps are the unit balancing isomorphisms. The reconstruction theorem identifies its total derived limit with Rhat_Y, proves derived completeness and identifies the canonical reductions with A_{n,Y}. The constant etale sheaves A_{n,Y} with their quotient maps give compatible etale-origin witnesses. These checks put L in the completed integral category on Y and give L_n=A_{n,Y}.

The maps gamma_n of Steps 2-3 identify M_n with Rf_n^!L_n, commute with their quotient transitions, and have a common single cohomological degree -2d. Apply case (b) of [lem-pur-condensed-exceptional-reconstruction]. Its single-degree clause supplies the actual identification of derived systems by functorial good truncation and the strict cohomology-diagram isomorphism; no arbitrary lift from evaluated isomorphisms is chosen. Thus all its hypotheses hold for this strict M_bullet and L. It gives c:U_X(M)->G(U_Y L), where G is exactly the target's chosen boundedConstructibleUpperShriek of Step 1. Here U_T is the functor defined in that theorem: first rationalize the completed Q_l lattice, realize by derived coefficient extension to E_T^c for E=Q_l, and extend coefficients to the finite-extension-valued B_T. Its conclusion includes the counit induced by completed reconstruction of the geometric finite counits. Thus it compares the actual chosen condensed right adjoint, not merely its object set or an unspecified exceptional functor. The theorem is applied to the finite adjoints that Step 2 explicitly identified with its own convention, and to their same counit mates verified in Step 3.

The unit comparison e_Y:U_Y L->B_Y is multiplication B_Y tensor^L_{Rhat_Y} Rhat_Y->B_Y, b tensor r |-> br, inverse b |-> b tensor 1. The K-flat ringed-site calculation [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] makes these maps the stated derived maps. Define a:G(B_Y)->U_X(M) by a=c^{-1} o G(e_Y^{-1}); its inverse is G(e_Y) o c. The functorial inverse equations prove that they are inverse. This obtains the required actual adjoint endpoint without substituting a finite-field common-stage adjunction for one over k.

source.place: Coherent finite unit tower, completed reconstruction and the exact condensed-adjoint comparison, case (b); this expands the unit case of the finite-to-adic-to-rational route

proof.text: Compare the integral ring in the actual Tate construction before comparing the twists. Write R_X=p_X^*C(-,Z_l) and A_{n,X}=(Z/ell^n)_X. The coefficient comparison [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] identifies R_X with lim_n A_{n,X}. It also identifies Q_{l,X} with R_X[1/ell] and B_X with colim_E E_X, along the specified coefficient inclusions. To check the quotient R_X/ell^n=A_{n,X}, use [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-point-basis-evaluation] on an affine weakly contractible V: the sections are C(S,Z_l), S=pi_0(|V|). A continuous map S->Z/ell^n has finitely many clopen fibres and lifts by choosing one Z_l lift of each value. A continuous Z_l-valued function zero modulo ell^n is uniquely ell^n times a continuous function (division by ell^n is continuous on ell^n Z_l). Thus the quotient and kernel have the claimed values on these V. They cover every site object by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-wcontractible-covering-family], so this is the sheaf quotient identification. With this identification the free internal module F_n=R_X tensor_Z mu_{ell^n,X} of [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists] is canonically mu_{ell^n,X}: since ell^n kills this sheaf, balancing factors through R_X/ell^n=A_{n,X}, and A_{n,X} tensor_{Z/ell^n} mu_{ell^n,X} -> mu_{ell^n,X} is multiplication with inverse z -> 1 tensor z. These maps intertwine 1 tensor (z->z^ell) with the power transition. It follows by the limit universal property that the target's T_X=lim_{n>=0}F_n is Z_l(1)_X=lim_{n>=1}mu_{ell^n,X}. The n=0 term is zero: a cone over positive levels extends uniquely by its zero map to that term, so including or deleting it does not change the limit.

source.place: Integral coefficient comparison; exact Tate construction in def-pur-condensed-tate-twists (archived master exhibit)

proof.text:
Finish the comparison with the exact target Tate construction. Write Z=Z_l(1)_X, R=Zhat_X=R_X as identified in Step 5. Step 4 and the derived-extension description of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] identify the ambient image of U_X(M) with B_X tensor^L_{E_X^c}(E_X^c tensor^L_R Z^{tensor_R d})[2d]. Here the coefficient inclusion R->B_X is the one through Q_l used in Step 4 and in [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists]. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], Z and its tensor powers are locally free of rank one over R. The flat-term K-flat computation of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the coefficient maps on the identity site, computes the displayed extension on this one-term flat complex. On a trivializing cover both successive extensions are extension of the rank-one coefficient module, so ordinary tensors compute them. The multiplication map b tensor (e tensor z) |-> be tensor z identifies the result with B_X tensor_R Z^{tensor_R d}, with inverse b tensor z |-> b tensor (1 tensor z). Balancing proves both inverse equations, and these maps glue since they use only the coefficient homomorphisms, not the choice of trivialization. Step 5 identifies the actual Tate module T_X with Z, with its power transitions and its level zero. Thus the actual target line L_X=B_X tensor_R T_X is B_X tensor_R Z. For d>=1 the canonical comparison
 (b_1 tensor z_1) tensor ... tensor (b_d tensor z_d) |-> (b_1...b_d) tensor (z_1 tensor ... tensor z_d)
from (B_X tensor_R Z)^{tensor_{B_X}d} to B_X tensor_R Z^{tensor_R d} has inverse
 b tensor (z_1 tensor ... tensor z_d) |-> (b tensor z_1) tensor (1 tensor z_2) tensor ... tensor (1 tensor z_d).
The balancing relations move every coefficient into the first factor, proving both inverse equations; all these are maps of sheaves and B_X-modules. For d=0 both modules are B_X and the comparison is the identity. Local freeness shows the same maps compute derived tensors. Apply the degree-zero inclusion and shift [2d]. By the exact definition [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists], this gives an ambient isomorphism b:iota_X(U_X(M))~=tateTwistDerived X ell d[2d]. This computes the actual module-object construction used by the target.

source.place: Unit-lattice coefficient extension and exact-master Tate line comparison: completed coefficients, bottom-field inclusion, balanced tensor powers and degree-zero inclusion

proof.text: Let iota_X:C^c(X)->D(Mod_{B_X}) be the full-subcategory inclusion. The required ambient isomorphism is b o iota_X(a), where a:G(B_Y)->U_X(M) is the explicitly typed isomorphism of Step 4 and b:iota_X U_X(M)->tateTwistDerived X ell d[2d] is the comparison of Step 6. Its inverse is iota_X(a^{-1}) o b^{-1}. Functoriality, associativity and the two constituent inverse equations prove both inverse equations. Its source is the ambient image of G(B_Y), with G exactly boundedConstructibleUpperShriek at the actual chosen compactification, and its target is exactly the upstream shifted Tate object. The source signature asks for chosen isomorphism data and imposes no additional base-change or composition equation.
